42886154.label: Background
42886154.text: Despite primary prevention statin treatment, a substantial proportion of individuals remain at residual risk for cardiovascular events. Coronary computed tomographic angiography (CTA) enables the quantification of compositional changes in calcified plaque.

42886154.label: Objectives
42886154.text: The aim of this study was to examine whether increases in coronary calcified plaque volume and density associated with statin therapy could be used as a marker of plaque stabilization in asymptomatic individuals undergoing serial coronary CTA.

42886154.label: Methods
42886154.text: In the CAUGHT-CAD trial, asymptomatic, statin-naive, intermediate-risk individuals were randomized to a primary prevention strategy (including statin treatment) vs usual care. Participants underwent coronary CTA at baseline and 3 years. In this post hoc analysis, volumes of 5 plaque subtypes were quantified: noncalcified (≤350 HU), low-density calcium (351-500 HU), intermediate-density calcium (501-700 HU), high-density calcium (701-1000 HU), and very high density calcium (>1,000 HU). The primary outcome was the per-lesion level change in volumes of calcified plaque subtypes.

42886154.label: Results
42886154.text: Eight hundred forty lesions were included from 338 participants (mean age: 58.3 ± 6.9 years, 57.1% men, 161 [47.6%] statin treated). Statin treatment was associated with greater progression in intermediate-density (β = 0.89, SE = 0.39; P = 0.02) and high-density (β = 0.79, SE = 0.24; P = 0.001) calcium, alongside regression of noncalcified plaque (β = -9.83, SE = 1.64; P < 0.001), following adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) level, and baseline plaque volume. Among statin-treated participants, LDL-C reduction ≥30% was associated with greater progression of high-density (β = 1.11, SE = 0.49; P = 0.03) and very high density (β = 1.68, SE = 0.85; P = 0.04) calcium.

42886154.label: Conclusions
42886154.text: In asymptomatic, intermediate-risk individuals, statin treatment was associated with a shift toward higher density calcium within coronary plaques, most marked with effective lowering of LDL-C.

42891704.label: Objectives
42891704.text: To compare structured and free-text MRI reporting in terms of objective report quality and surgeon ratings of perceived clinical utility in suspected deep pelvic endometriosis.

42891704.label: Materials and methods
42891704.text: In this single-center randomized reader study, 20 radiology residents were assigned to free-text or structured reporting. Five residents became unavailable before report generation and provided no outcome data. The remaining 15 readers completed the same 22 pelvic MRI examinations, generating 330 reports: 154 free-text and 176 structured reports. Reports were compared with an imaging reference standard established by two pelvic radiologists through independent review and consensus adjudication. The primary endpoint was clinically weighted completeness. Secondary endpoints included unweighted completeness, explicit negative discrepancies relative to the expert imaging reference, positive findings unsupported by the expert imaging reference, and reporting time. Objective outcomes were analyzed using mixed-effects models or Poisson generalized estimating equations. In an exploratory paired assessment, two expert gynecologic surgeons evaluated 44 reports, comprising one free-text and one structured report for each MRI examination.

42891704.label: Results
42891704.text: Structured reporting was associated with an 8.1%-point increase in completeness compared with free-text reporting (95% CI, 4.1-12.1; p < 0.001) and a 5.6%-point increase in clinically weighted completeness (95% CI, 1.3-10.0; p = 0.011). Reporting time was 4.52 min longer with structured reporting (95% CI, 3.05-5.99; p < 0.001). Structured reporting was also associated with more explicit negative discrepancies relative to the expert imaging reference (rate ratio, 2.94; 95% CI, 1.73-4.98; p < 0.001). These discrepancies were mainly explicit compartment-based negative statements. In the exploratory surgeon assessment, structured reports received higher ratings for perceived completeness, usefulness for clinical decision-making, and adequacy to clinical needs, whereas clarity ratings were similar between formats.

42891704.label: Conclusion
42891704.text: Structured MRI reporting was associated with higher objective completeness and, in an exploratory assessment, higher surgeon ratings for several dimensions of perceived clinical utility. These findings should be balanced against longer reporting time and more explicit negative discrepancies relative to the expert imaging reference.

42925454.label: Background
42925454.text: Quantitative imaging of cerebral blood flow (CBF), oxygen extraction fraction (OEF), cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO2), and cerebral blood volume (CBV) using 15O-labeled compounds is useful for evaluating cerebral ischemia. However, quantitative PET requires measurement of blood activity concentration, which is typically obtained by arterial blood sampling. Although image-derived and reference-based input function methods have been developed for CBF, OEF, and CMRO2 quantification, a non-invasive method for obtaining blood activity concentration for CBV measurement has not been established. This study aimed to develop and validate a reference-based method for estimating blood activity concentration from C15O PET images.

42925454.label: Methods
42925454.text: Among 186 subjects, mean CBV and the coefficient of variation (CV) were calculated for each brain segment in 64 subjects (Group A; moyamoya disease (MMD) present/absent, 20/44). In an independent cohort of 122 subjects (Group B; MMD present/absent, 35/87), blood activity concentration was estimated for each brain segment by reproducing the reference mean CBV obtained from Group A. The segment-based estimates were combined using CV-weighted averaging. The estimated blood activity concentrations were compared with those obtained by arterial blood sampling.

42925454.label: Results
42925454.text: The mean ± SD of CBV across all segments in Group A was 0.039 ± 0.011 ml/g overall, 0.037 ± 0.009 ml/g in subjects without MMD, and 0.043 ± 0.012 ml/g in subjects with MMD. In Group B, the percentage differences between reference-based and measured blood activity concentrations were 0.35 ± 9.8%, -1.4 ± 8.8%, and 4.8 ± 10.6% in the overall, MMD-absent, and MMD-present groups, respectively, using the all-segment approach. When the CBV-matched segment approach was applied, the corresponding differences were -0.60 ± 8.8%, -1.4 ± 8.4%, and 1.5 ± 9.4%, respectively.

42925454.label: Conclusions
42925454.text: The reference-based blood activity concentrations showed good agreement with those obtained by arterial blood sampling, and the CBV-matched segment approach reduced the difference in the MMD-present group. The proposed method may enable non-invasive and automated estimation of blood activity concentration for quantitative CBV measurement without arterial blood sampling.

42933554.label: Objective
42933554.text: To evaluate the long-term diagnostic performance and consistency of a dedicated sonographer-performed thyroid FNAB program under radiologist supervision.

42933554.label: Materials and methods
42933554.text: This retrospective quality improvement study (QIRC 23-0591) analyzed consecutive thyroid FNABs performed between 2008 and 2022 at a single academic center. A structured sonographer training program was implemented in 2011. Biopsies were categorized into three periods: pre-implementation (2008-April 2011), early post-implementation (August 2011-2013), and late post-implementation (2014-2022). FNABs performed by other clinicians during the late implementation period served as a contemporaneous control group. Outcomes were assessed at the nodule level using the Bethesda System for Reporting Thyroid Cytopathology. Trend analyses were performed using the Cochran-Armitage test; chi-square tests compared groups.

42933554.label: Results
42933554.text: A total of 14,127 thyroid nodules were biopsied in the radiology (4,382 pre-implementation; 2,561 early post-implementation; 7,184 late post-implementation period). Nondiagnostic rates decreased from 34% (1492/4382) pre-implementation to 21% (534/2561) early post-implementation and 8.6% (617/7184) late post-implementation period (p<.001). Malignant cytology increased from 4.9% to 5.6% to 7.7%, and combined Bethesda V/VI diagnoses increased from 8.9% to 8.5% to 12.1% (both p<.001). During late post-implementation period, sonographer-performed FNABs demonstrated lower nondiagnostic rates (8.6% vs 29%, p<.001) and higher malignant yield (7.6% vs 4.5%, p<.001) compared with other clinicians. Adoption of ACR TI-RADS in 2020 was not associated with significant changes in adequacy or malignancy rates.

42933554.label: Conclusions
42933554.text: A dedicated sonographer-performed thyroid FNAB program improved diagnostic adequacy and malignancy yield over 11 years, supporting safe delegation of thyroid FNAB to trained physician extenders under radiologist supervision.

42957204.text: Radiolabeled fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeting peptides, such as 90Y-FAPI-46, have increasingly been used to treat various tumor entities, with preliminary reports indicating therapeutic responses with acceptable toxicity profiles. Dosimetry can be used to maximize antitumor capability and minimize side effects. The aim of this study was to investigate whether 90Y-FAPI-46 tumor dosimetry can be predicted by diagnostic 68Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT data. Methods: Fourteen patients with 24 lesions underwent a single-time-point 68Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT scan and 3 90Y-FAPI-46 PET/CT scans for dosimetry within a 3-mo interval. Tumors were identified on PET images, and the anatomic tumor volume was measured on low-dose CT. Tumor uptake extrapolated at time of injection, time-integrated activity coefficient (TIAC), and tumor absorbed dose were calculated as reference values using 90Y-FAPI-46 data and compared with the corresponding predicted values using 68Ga-FAPI-46 data by means of a single-time-point dosimetry model. Correlations between 90Y-FAPI-46- and 68Ga-FAPI-46-based values were assessed. Results: In calculating the predicted values using a single-time-point 68Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT, the mean effective half-life of 90Y-FAPI-46 across all lesions was 8.44 ± 1.73 h. The mean ± SD ratio (i.e., the predicted values using 68Ga-FAPI-46 data divided by the reference 90Y-FAPI-46 data) were 0.93 ± 0.39, 0.77 ± 0.35, and 0.77 ± 0.35 for tumor uptake, TIAC, and tumor absorbed dose, respectively. In the Bland-Altman analysis, mean differences (bias) ± SD of the percent differences of tumor uptake, TIAC, and tumor absorbed dose were -16.11% ± 43.28% (95% CI, -100.90 to 68.73%; Spearman ρ = 0.91; P < 0.0001), -32.60% ± 41.26% (95% CI, -113.50 to 48.26%; Spearman ρ = 0.91; P < 0.0001), and -33.35% ± 40.19% (95% CI, -112.10 to 45.43%; Spearman ρ = 0.77; P < 0.0001), respectively. Conclusion: Tumor uptake, TIAC, and tumor absorbed dose on 90Y-FAPI-46 PET/CT and 68Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT were highly correlated, although the values on 68Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT tended to be lower than those on 90Y-FAPI-46 PET/CT. Predicted values on 68Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT can help clinicians with diagnostic stratification and patient selection, with intratherapeutic verification remaining necessary before any individualization of administered activity.

43018704.text: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is an important predictive and prognostic biomarker that guides targeted therapy, particularly in breast and gastric cancers. Conventional HER2 assessment using immunohistochemistry (IHC) and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) is limited by inter-observer variability, heterogeneous expression, and diagnostic complexity. This systematic review and diagnostic meta-analysis followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines to evaluate Artificial Intelligence-based HER2 assessment. Fifty-one studies were included in the qualitative synthesis and 14 in the diagnostic meta-analysis. Bibliometric analysis, methodological taxonomy, comparative evaluation, and pooled diagnostic performance were assessed, with study quality evaluated using QUADAS-2. AI methodologies have rapidly evolved from conventional machine learning and radiomics to deep learning, Vision Transformers, explainable AI, and multimodal frameworks, with histopathology and Magnetic Resonance Imaging. being the most frequently used modalities. Research activity increased markedly between 2023 and 2025. Pooled sensitivity was 87.8%, specificity was 83.5%, and Summary Receiver Operating Characteristic Area Under the Curve (SROC AUC) was 0.852 (95% CI: 0.801-0.881), indicating promising overall diagnostic performance. Deeks' funnel plot asymmetry test showed no significant evidence of publication bias (p = 0.14). However, heterogeneity warrants cautious interpretation of the pooled estimates. Heterogeneous datasets, limited external validation, and inconsistent evaluation methods remain important barriers to clinical implementation. Future research should emphasize multicenter prospective validation, explainable and multimodal AI, foundation models, federated learning, and evaluation in underexplored malignancies, including gallbladder cancer.

43024054.text: Cystic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (c-PanNETs) are an uncommon cystic phenotype of well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, accounting for approximately 7-12% of PanNETs in several surgical series, although reported frequencies vary according to the definition of cystic morphology and cohort selection. Retrospective studies suggest that c-PanNETs may exhibit less aggressive clinicopathologic features than their solid counterparts; however, their imaging appearance frequently overlaps with other pancreatic cystic neoplasms, particularly branch-duct intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms, mucinous cystic neoplasms, and atypical serous cystic neoplasms. Accurate preoperative recognition may have important implications for patient management and surgical planning. This review summarizes the imaging features of c-PanNETs across computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography, as well as the complementary roles of endoscopic ultrasound and somatostatin receptor PET/CT. Particular attention is given to arterial hyperenhancement of the cyst wall, septations, mural nodules, or residual solid components; assessment of communication with the main pancreatic duct; and integration of complementary imaging findings. Because these features are not specific, their interpretation in combination with lesion morphology and ductal relationships is emphasized. Practical approaches to differential diagnosis and common interpretive pitfalls are also discussed. The review further addresses emerging quantitative imaging techniques, including radiomics and artificial intelligence, while recognizing that evidence specific to c-PanNETs remains limited. A practical diagnostic algorithm and structured reporting checklist are provided to support systematic interpretation and multidisciplinary communication. Recognition of the imaging spectrum of c-PanNETs, combined with systematic assessment of enhancement characteristics, ductal anatomy, and complementary imaging findings, may improve diagnostic confidence and support appropriate patient management.
